title: Host genomic context determines the direction of an oracle-predicted sequence effect: a composition-preserving CpG intervention in Enformer and Borzoi.
authors: Uysal, Selahattin Alperen
abstract: Sequence-to-function models are increasingly used as oracles to score designed regulatory elements, on the untested assumption that an effect measured at one locus holds at another. Taking chromatin and host loci from multiple sclerosis risk regions, we kept four questions apart: sequence realism, transfer of discrimination, edit stability, calibration. A sixth-order Markov chain reproduced the cell-type-specific motif enrichment a trained transformer missed, despite its lower held-out likelihood. Scores differ in level between loci far more than between inserts at one locus, yet inserts selected by an Enformer-derived index kept 85% of their advantage at four unseen loci. Once GC was matched, however, the index separated peak-derived from inaccessible sequence at none of 12 hosts, and from random sequence in opposite directions at different hosts. Placing identical inserts and an identical CpG edit at 24 host loci, the effect varied far beyond sampling noise on host identity alone ([Formula: see text]), unpredicted by 18 host properties. It survives scoring only the bins the insert occupies ([Formula: see text], and across 200 loci), so is no artefact of aggregation; the apparent host dominance, however, falls from 25-fold to 3-fold under that localised score, and the one locus positive under the whole-window score reverses under it. Borzoi reproduced the heterogeneity but not its amplitude, and the objective did not predict lentiMPRA activity. For these two oracles and this edit, the size of a predicted effect depends on where it is measured, and its direction at any one locus is not robust.

title: Cross-task benchmarking reveals variable transferability of deep learning models across molecular quantitative trait loci.
authors: Chen, Sihan; Wang, Xiaoyu; Peleg, Anton Y; Xu, Shuting; Li, Fuyi; Webb, Geoffrey I; Song, Jiangning
abstract: Most genetic variants associated with complex traits reside in non-coding regions of the genome, complicating their functional interpretation. Recent deep learning models have advanced the prediction of expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs), but whether these models generalize across diverse molecular phenotypes is unknown. Here, we assess the cross-task transferability of pretrained regulatory features from six representative sequence- and annotation-based models across nine classes of molecular quantitative trait loci (xQTLs). We observe that while all models perform well in eQTL prediction, their performance varies substantially across other xQTL predictions. Chromatin accessibility, transcription factor binding, and histone QTLs are generally well predicted, whereas chromatin looping and microRNA expression QTLs remain challenging. Foundation models, particularly AlphaGenome and Borzoi, consistently outperform models based on local sequence context and exhibit improved robustness across class-imbalance settings. Tree-based ensemble classifiers further enhance predictive performance, suggesting that nonlinear interactions among regulatory features contribute substantially to variant prioritization. Applying AlphaGenome and Borzoi to coronary artery disease-associated genome-wide association studies loci identifies 337 high-confidence candidate chromatin accessibility QTLs, including 11 previously reported and 326 candidates that display significantly larger allele-specific differences in predicted chromatin accessibility signals. Collectively, our results reveal substantial variability in the cross-task performance of current eQTL-centric models, highlight the advantages of long-range genomic representations and inform the prioritization of candidate regulatory variants contributing to complex diseases.

title: Data analysis of experimentally solved nucleosome arrays reveals heterogeneous features.
authors: Portillo-Ledesma, Stephanie; Li, Zilong; Franowicz, Elijah; Schlick, Tamar
abstract: Atomic-resolution nucleosome array structures have provided invaluable information on eukaryotic genome packing. Although these arrays are often obtained for regular fibers with designed sequences, such information complements in vivo genome organization data and modeling studies. Here, we analyze such systems with a focus on chromatin organization. We highlight both robust and unique features, as well as suitable average values for coarse-grained modeling, such as the relative orientation and positioning of neighboring nucleosomes, and opening of the linker DNA. Our associated web resource (https://www.biomath.nyu.edu/chromstruct/) shares these collected systems and provides tools for their analysis. The heterogeneous features exhibit a wide range of geometrical properties that depend on linker DNA length, core histone protein variants, auxiliary protein binding, and fiber interdigitation. Yet experimental fiber geometries can be reproduced reasonably using average parameters, as demonstrated here by simulations with our mesoscale model for regular fibers and as reported separately for life-like systems with epigenetic marks. Such analysis may also be useful for modular design of chromatin fibers. The structural characterization of these chromatin building blocks provides new insights into the regulation of chromatin architecture and has implications for the modular design of chromatin fibers.

title: GECSI: large-scale chromatin state imputation from gene expression.
authors: Fu, Jingyuan; Ernst, Jason
abstract: Chromatin state annotations based on epigenetic marks are powerful resources, but many additional samples have gene expression data available while lacking epigenetic mark data and chromatin state annotations. Using the EpiATLAS resource of the International Human Epigenome Consortium (IHEC), we develop Gene Expression-based Chromatin State Imputation (GECSI), which uses an ensemble of multi-class logistic regression classifiers to predict chromatin state annotations from gene expression data. We show in cross-validation that GECSI accurately predicts observed chromatin state annotations. We also apply GECSI using gene expression data in 449 IHEC additional samples, providing an expanded chromatin state annotation resource.

title: Charge-altering histone mutations reprogram electrostatic coupling from single nucleosomes to higher-order chromatin structures.
authors: Zhang, Houfang; Hu, Guanhua; Liu, Gege; Xu, Wang; Zhao, Xinyi; Li, Anbang; Peng, Yunhui
abstract: Nucleosomes are stabilized and organized by electrostatic interactions that govern chromatin folding and higher-order structure. Although many cancer-associated histone mutations alter residue charge, how such perturbations propagate from single nucleosomes to higher-order chromatin organization remains unclear. Here, through large-scale analysis of histone mutation datasets, we show that charge-altering mutations are enriched among recurrent high-frequency mutations and exhibit stronger predicted destabilizing effects on nucleosome-associated interactions than charge-neutral variants. We demonstrate that even a single charge-altering mutation can substantially reshape the nucleosome surface electrostatic potential, thereby modulating long-range electrostatic interactions with regulatory proteins. By systematically analyzing 25 experimentally resolved nucleosome-protein complexes and 183 mutant models, we quantify how individual charge-altering mutations substantially alter electrostatic interaction forces. Extensive molecular dynamics simulations totaling 18 mus further reveal that single-point mutations can produce less favorable nucleosome-protein binding-energy estimates and reorganize interfacial hydrogen-bonding networks. Importantly, analysis of higher-order nucleosome assemblies shows that charge-altering mutations can modulate inter-nucleosomal electrostatic interactions in a packing-geometry-dependent manner, while mutations near the acidic patch can also perturb H4 tail-nucleosome electrostatic coupling. Our results provide a physical framework for understanding how local electrostatic perturbations caused by cancer-associated charge-altering histone mutations may influence nucleosome interactions across multiple structural scales.

title: Genome-Wide and Multi-Omics Analysis Identified DNA-Interacting Circular RNA circFOXK2 as MLL1 Regulator for Histone H3K4 Methylation in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
authors: Wong, Chi Hin; Pena-Paladines, Jessica Jazmin; Leung, Sum Yin Valerie; To, Ka-Fai; Chok, Kenneth Siu Ho; Chen, Yangchao
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most devastating malignancies with high lethality despite the current therapeutic interventions. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) play important roles in many biological processes and disease development. However, the underlying mechanism remains largely unexplored. To identify novel druggable targets, we aimed to elucidate the mechanisms contributing to the critical roles of circRNAs in PDAC. We performed a genome-wide and multi-omics investigation on the circFOXK2-DNA interaction in PDAC progression. Single-cell ATAC-sequencing analysis using the publicly available dataset revealed the importance of the circFOXK2-DNA interaction network in intratumoral heterogeneity. Through circRNA-DNA interaction by complementary base pairing, circFOXK2 recognizes targets at different genomic locations: enhancer, promoter, and intragenic region. CircFOXK2 forms a docking pocket by intramolecular base pairing for the N-terminal RNA-recognition motif of PPIE, disrupting the PPIE-MLL1 interaction. This removes the PPIE inhibitory effects on MLL1 for gene-activating H3K4 methylation. Specifically, circFOXK2 promotes TMSB15B and BCAS1 expressions by enhancing H3K4me3 at the promoter. At the gene body, circFOXK2 facilitates transcription elongation of TRIO and LAMA4 by intragenic H3K4me3. At the distal intergenic enhancer, circFOXK2 promotes H3K4me1 of CYP26A1 and TCP11 for gene activation. These results highlight the importance and therapeutic potential of circRNA-DNA interaction in gene regulation.

title: Identification of ageing-related genes in prostate cancer with type 2 Diabetes using machine learning: a multi-omics study focusing on SOX4, PRNP, and FOXO4.
authors: Zhang, Wei; Zhang, Xueqian; Zhang, Chenghao; Shi, Xinyang; Deng, Yiheng; Gao, Yan; Bi, Kaipeng; Wang, Zheng; Chen, Guanqiu; Ye, Zhoujie; An, Ziyan; Fu, Weijun
abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) demonstrates complex associations with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and ageing, though their interconnected molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. This study aimed to identify and validate diagnostic biomarkers at the intersection of these pathways to enable early detection and risk stratification in high-risk populations. Bioinformatic analysis was performed on PCa and T2DM transcriptomic data downloaded from the GEO database, followed by differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and functional enrichment. Eight machine learning algorithms were applied to identify hub ageing-related genes (ARGs), with SHAP analysis interpreting feature importance. A nomogram model was constructed and validated across multiple cohorts. Immune infiltration, drug sensitivity, single-cell RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomics were used for mechanistic exploration. Three key ARGs (SOX4, PRNP, and FOXO4) were identified and used to develop a diagnostic model with high accuracy (AUCs: 0.726-0.905). SOX4 promoted immune evasion, PRNP exhibited context-dependent duality, and FOXO4 functioned as a tumor suppressor. Spatial and single-cell analyses revealed cell-type-specific expression and fibroblast-epithelial communication via MIF, LRP1, and FZD1. Drug sensitivity profiling identified abiraterone and docetaxel as potential therapeutics for high- and low-risk patients, respectively. In conclusion, SOX4, PRNP, and FOXO4 are key biomarkers linking PCa, T2DM, and ageing, and the diagnostic model shows robust performance and clinical utility, providing insights into microenvironment-driven mechanisms and personalized treatment strategies for PCa patients with T2DM.

title: Genetic variants shape single-cell chromatin accessibility and disease risk.
authors: Xue, Angli; Fan, Jianan; Dong, Oscar A; Huang, Hao Lawrence; Chen, Ling; Allen, Peter C; Spenceley, Eleanor; Sagi-Zsigmond, Eszter; Bowen, Blake; Henry, Albert; Cuomo, Anna S E; Tanudisastro, Hope A; Qiao, Zhen; Dorans, Elizabeth; Ben-David, Eyal; Farh, Kyle Kai-How; Hu, Linfeng; Liu, Yijia Christiana; Neavin, Drew R; Lee, Arthur S; Senabouth, Anne; Bartie, Caitlin; McCloy, Rachael A; Chin, Venessa; Zhou, Wei; Price, Alkes L; de Lange, Katrina M; Figtree, Gemma A; Hewitt, Alex W; MacArthur, Daniel G; Powell, Joseph E
abstract: Understanding how genetic variation shapes gene regulation at single-cell resolution is crucial for elucidating complex disease mechanisms(1), but has been limited by the lack of large-scale single-cell multi-omics data(2-4). Here we present single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing of 3.5 million peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 1,042 donors with matched whole-genome sequencing. Across 28 immune cell types, we tested 440,996 chromatin accessibility peaks and identified 243,225 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) at 100,483 peaks, 60% of them cell-type specific. Rare variant analysis identified 38,161 associated peaks, with predicted transcription factor-binding disruption implicated at individual loci. Colocalization with expression QTLs (eQTLs) from single-cell RNA sequencing data (5.4 million peripheral blood mononuclear cells)(5) defined 28,834 candidate cis-regulatory elements. Across genome-wide association studies for 16 diseases and 44 blood traits, caQTLs colocalized 4.5-22.6% more signals than eQTLs alone. Cell-type-specific and tissue-specific context, distal effects and multi-causal-variant models raised genome-wide association study-eQTL concordance from approximately 16% to approximately 65%. Cell state further modulates genetic effects, with 27% of over 200,000 caQTL-cell-state interactions lacking a main effect. At the inflammatory bowel disease risk gene ADCY7, accessibility effects varied with genotype and G protein-mediated pathway activity in CD4(+) T cells. A graph neural network trained on both eQTL and caQTL layers inferred peak-gene links in unpaired multiome data with up to 17.2% higher accuracy than QTL-agnostic data, uncovering 128 additional transcription factor-target pairs (22% increase). Together, these results show that genetic variants shape chromatin accessibility in a cell-type-specific and cell-state-specific manner, influencing immune function and disease risk.

title: A systematic delineation of 3'UTR regulatory elements and their contextual associations.
authors: Liang, Nan; Li, Jing-Yi; Ding, Yang; Wang, Yu; Champer, Jackson; Ren, Li-Chen; Gao, Ge
abstract: The 3'UTR encodes regulatory information that shapes transcript abundance and subcellular distribution, yet the underlying sequence rules remain incompletely defined. We quantified the effects of  approximately 2 million synthetic 3'UTR inserts in A549 and HCT116 cells on RNA output and nuclear-cytoplasmic partitioning. We identified a broad repertoire of short 2- to 8-nt elements. Their effects largely followed a dominant coupled axis linking high RNA output with cytoplasmic enrichment and low RNA output with nuclear enrichment and were predominantly additive. A context-aware deep learning model captures most of this behavior while revealing that strong context dependence is uncommon and emerges mainly in rare, extreme contexts consistent with higher-order constraints. Applying the model to ClinVar 3'UTR variants prioritizes a subset of pathogenic single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) with aberrant predicted effects, frequently explained by creation or disruption of splice-site-like U1 motifs that can trigger telescripting-associated readthrough, highlighting a potent route to 3'UTR-driven disease mechanisms. A record of this paper's transparent peer review process is included in the supplemental information.

title: XChrom: A Cross-Cell Chromatin Accessibility Prediction Model Integrating Genomic Sequence and Cellular Context.
authors: Miao, Yuanyuan; Liang, Xuan; Zhang, Wenwen; Han, Dongmei; Li, Yurun; Wang, Zhen
abstract: Single-cell chromatin accessibility offers unique insights into transcriptional regulation beyond gene expression. However, paired datasets of these two modalities remain relatively scarce, and existing computational models cannot simultaneously predict chromatin accessibility for unseen genomic regions and cells. Here, we present XChrom, a deep learning framework for genome-wide cross-cell chromatin accessibility prediction that integrates genomic sequence and single-cell transcriptomics-derived cell identity into a unified model. Comprehensive evaluations show that XChrom consistently outperforms existing methods in cross-region and cross-cell predictions, and uniquely enables cross-both predictions. It also supports cross-sample prediction when batch effects are properly corrected. Cross-species analyses demonstrate XChrom's robust performance and its ability to capture evolutionarily conserved regulatory rules. Applied to peripheral blood mononuclear cells from COVID-19 patients, XChrom accurately identifies transcription factor activities in novel but related cell states and reveals pathogenesis-associated regulatory alterations. XChrom is available as an open-source Python package, facilitating single-cell transcriptional regulation research.

title: An extensible deep learning framework for multi-type chromatin interaction prediction through hierarchical adaptation strategies.
authors: Wang, Shuaibin; Chen, Tong; Liu, Weixu; Zheng, Xuejie; Yang, Zhongxin; Liang, Zhen; Shen, Yin
abstract: Three-dimensional chromatin interactions play essential roles in gene regulation, yet computational prediction of diverse interaction types remains largely dependent on specialized, single-task models. Here, we present UniLoopNet, a multi-task deep learning framework that predicts multiple types of chromatin interactions including enhancer-promoter interactions, enhancer-enhancer interactions, CTCF-mediated loops, and stripe-associated interactions from DNA sequences. UniLoopNet employs a shared encoder-decoder architecture with hierarchical adaptation strategies, integrating multi-task, transfer, and continual learning based on task semantic similarity. Comprehensive benchmarking across multiple cell lines demonstrates that UniLoopNet outperforms existing specialized and multi-task approaches, with AUROCs exceeding 0.90 in most tasks. Under stringent evaluation settings, including chromosome-matched, distance-matched, realistic imbalanced, and locus-disjoint tests, AUROCs range from 0.8934 to 0.9366. In the realistic 1:5 class-imbalance setting, the AUPRCs for enhancer-promoter and enhancer-enhancer interaction prediction are 0.7956 and 0.6935, respectively. Cross-cell-line transfer experiments further show that applying UniLoopNet to another cell line requires adaptation by supervised fine-tuning on target-cell-line data, after which performance is comparable to that of within-cell-line training. Notably, the framework exhibits data efficiency in experiments with substantially reduced training data. Interpretability analyses reveal that the learned sequence features are associated with known transcription factor binding sites and uncover differential regulatory effects of disease-associated variants. UniLoopNet provides a versatile and data-efficient framework for sequence-based prediction and interpretation of diverse 3D genome interactions, complementing existing sequence-to-map approaches while improving the understanding of sequence-encoded regulatory potential.

title: DNA Geometry Around Highly Transcribed Bacterial Genes.
authors: Joyeux, Marc
abstract: Recent high-resolution ( approximately 500 bp) Hi-C experiments reported contact maps with unusual patterns around highly expressed bacterial DNA loci. These patterns, described as "arched stripes" and "bundled domains", extend over nearly 100 kbp. We performed Brownian Dynamics simulations with a specially designed coarse-grained model to rationalize these findings. The main feature of the model is that it takes explicitly into account the waves of positive (respectively, negative) supercoiling generated by the translocating polymerase downstream (respectively, upstream) of its position. Contact maps computed from the simulations also display the arched stripe and bundled domain patterns for above-threshold values of the rate of twist injection. Computed DNA conformations indicate that these patterns reflect an extraordinarily entangled DNA geometry, which involves both plectonemic and toroidal supercoiling, with some DNA segments experiencing both of them simultaneously. Moreover, DNA segments located on each side of the polymerase systematically wind around tracts located on the other side, which is a purely out-of-equilibrium effect driven by the continuous injection of twist. The present work therefore reveals that repeated transcription of a DNA locus systematically brings into contact DNA segments separated by several tens of kbp, which may eventually contribute to allosteric modulation and long-range communication.

title: A Frozen Plant DNA Language Model for Computational Prioritization and Functional Annotation of Melon (Cucumis melo) Variants.
authors: Sun, Guosheng; Wei, Yanping; Li, Entong; Xiao, Mengting; Zhang, Zhilin; Zhang, Zhenchao; Dai, Zhongliang; Ma, Zhihu; Zhang, Changwei
abstract: Background/Objectives: Fruit quality in melon is determined by complex traits including sugar accumulation, aroma, flesh color, ripening behavior and disease resistance. Conventional genomic selection provides limited mechanistic interpretation, especially for regulatory and de novo variants. We adapted the EVEE interpretable embedding-probing framework to melon using PlantCAD2 as a frozen DNA language model backbone. Methods: The model was not fine-tuned or further pre-trained. Instead, lightweight probes were trained on fixed embeddings derived from sequence windows surrounding genetic variants. The pipeline integrated supervised variant-effect prediction, functional perturbation profiling, training-free masked log-likelihood ratio scoring, and cis-regulatory element generation. We applied the framework to 32,268 public genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS) SNPs from a melon diversity panel. A total of 30,052 variants were successfully encoded and analyzed. Results: Of these, 31.9% were classified as high predicted functional effect under the GWAS-proximal probe. We adopted a rigorous independent split based on chromosome and locus blocks to ensure test variants and training variants occupy distinct linkage-disequilibrium blocks. In this setting, the covariance probe yields an AUROC of approximately 0.51 with a 95% confidence interval covering 0.50, indicating no predictive advantage over random guessing. The full-cohort AUROC value of 0.748 reported earlier is attributed to linkage-disequilibrium leakage and overlapping positive samples between datasets, and thus does not reflect true independent generalization. The 17-class structural annotation probe reached 95.97% per-position accuracy. Functional perturbation signals were enriched in intronic, coding, and proximal promoter regions, consistent with known regulatory architectures in melon. Using the masked language model head with Gibbs sampling, we generated 76 candidate 400 bp cis-regulatory elements associated with sugar metabolism pathways. A posterior consistency check against 18 published GWAS/QTL loci showed effect-score patterns broadly concordant with reported loci; this is a consistency analysis against known loci, not an independent prospective validation. Variants in the CmTST2 region exhibited elevated mean effect scores of 0.7922 compared with the genome-wide background of 0.406. Conclusions: Overall, this study provides a computational, hypothesis-generating framework in which a frozen plant DNA language model combined with lightweight probes prioritizes melon variants and generates candidate regulatory sequences; all outputs are unverified in-silico predictions requiring experimental validation before any functional or breeding use. Because every variant is scored independently from its local sequence context, the framework necessarily treats genetically linked, network-dependent traits as single-locus effects and does not model epistasis, pathway-level interactions, or genotype-by-environment effects; the outputs are sequence-level priors, not phenotype predictions. The results support a generalizable framework for model-guided functional genomics and precision breeding in Cucurbitaceae crops.

title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals distinct regulatory architectures coordinating carbon assimilation and cyclic electron flow in maize C(4) photosynthesis.
authors: Li, Chuanshun; Zhang, You; Lin, Kande; Liu, Xiaojian; Zhang, Hanxiao; Yang, Jianzhao; Zhao, Caiyao; Yang, Leyi; Long, Zhengbiao; Li, Yangmeihui; Deng, Qilin; Ma, Bin; Wei, Tong; Zhong, Silin; Zhu, Xinguang; Li, Pinghua; Pan, Xiaoyong; Tu, Xiaoyu
abstract: C(4) photosynthesis arose repeatedly through redeployment of pre-existing regulatory circuitry, yet how a shared regulatory system coordinates its interdependent photosynthetic functions remains unresolved. Here we integrate single-nucleus RNA-seq and sci-ATAC-seq with bulk histone profiles from mesophyll- and bundle sheath-enriched fractions and transcription factor binding profiles obtained in protoplasts. We compare the C(4) shuttle and Calvin-Benson-Bassham cycle with NDH-mediated cyclic electron flow in bundle sheath cells. Selected carbon assimilation loci were associated with differential H3K27me3, whereas the NDH-associated branch showed regulatory inputs linked to DNA binding with one finger (DOF) transcription factors. Dissection of the ZmNdhU promoter identifies a 49 bp DOF-responsive cis element whose activity is sensitive to local sequence context and insertion position in the promoter constructs tested and that supports vascular bundle-associated reporter expression in a heterologous promoter context. Bundle sheath-enriched expression of ZmDOF30 increases NDH-associated expression, cyclic electron flow, leaf ATP content and photosynthetic performance. In a field trial, the transgenic lines showed increased growth and biomass. Comparative analyses revealed lineage-associated variation in predicted promoter-proximal DOF-binding potential within a broader H3K27me3-associated transcription factor background. These findings distinguish regulatory configurations among maize photosynthetic modules and identify DOF-NDH regulation as a candidate route for improving photosynthetic performance in maize, with broader relevance to NADP-ME grasses.

title: A droplet-based long-read single-cell epigenome sequencing method for the high-throughput profiling of multidimensional regulatory elements within individual cells.
authors: Lu, Jiansen; Chen, Kexuan; Jia, Shengtao; Chen, Guodong; Yu, Xianhong; Li, Wen
abstract: Recently, long-read sequencing methods have revolutionized genomic research by allowing the resolution of previously inaccessible regions across the genome. However, the throughput and scalability of these methods have hindered their general application in the field. To address this limitation, we developed droplet-based methods for the single-cell profiling of chromatin accessibility (droplet-based single-cell Nanopore ATAC-seq, dscNanoATAC) and histone modifications (droplet-based single-cell NanoCUT&Tag, dscNanoCUT) by combining a commercial microfluidic device and long-read sequencing platform, achieving a throughput of ~5000 cells in a single experiment and significantly reducing the time and costs compared with previous techniques. With cultured mammalian cells, we demonstrated the ability of dscNanoATAC and dscNanoCUT to detect allele-specific epigenetics, neighboring co-accessibility, and regulatory elements within low-mappability regions. Furthermore, leveraging the haplotype-resolved data generated from dscNanoATAC, we optimized a deep-learning model to predict allele-specific three-dimensional genome structures with high resolution (10 kb). We also applied dscNanoATAC and dscNanoCUT in complex tissues using the mouse brain as an example, and characterized the allele-specific regulation of the imprinting gene Ube3a in neurons, obtaining insights into the mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of Prader-Willi and Angelman syndrome. With dscNanoCUT, we systematically evaluated the activity of transposon elements and revealed their potential regulatory functions in the mouse brain. Together, dscNanoATAC and dscNanoCUT serve as a versatile and scalable long-read epigenome sequencing platform, enabling multidimensional analyses of elements ranging from chromatin accessibility to histone modifications and their interplay between chromatin structures. This platform may advance our understanding of epigenetic regulation in complex biological systems.

title: EpiInsula: calibrated regression of the Hi-C insulation score from cell-type-specific epigenomic signal.
authors: Jin, Yuyu; Chen, Tong; Gao, Jie; Tong, Mengyao; Xu, Guangcheng; Zhang, Xueyu; Liu, Weixu; Shen, Yin
abstract: Chromatin insulation shapes which regulatory elements can reach which promoters, but much computational prediction of chromatin organisation has been posed as boundary classification, which discards the depth and shape of the insulation profile. We developed EpiInsula, a dilated convolutional framework that predicts the 10-kb Hi-C insulation score as a continuous quantity from six cell-type-specific epigenomic tracks read over a +/-700-kb window. Under a chromosome-disjoint partition that scores every evaluated locus with a model which never saw its chromosome, held-out correlations across four human cell lines are 0.791, 0.780, 0.860 and 0.774, and the regression of measured on predicted insulation has slopes of 0.90-0.95, indicating calibration of the conditional mean, the sense used throughout. Against seven methods fitted under a single evaluation contract, EpiInsula gives the highest correlation and, with boundary thresholds selected on validation chromosomes and frozen before testing, the highest boundary F1 against 4D Nucleome calls in every cell line; the lead is retained on the fine-scale component of the profile, and three published contact-map predictors retrained on the same data give lower correlation on the derived insulation score. On boundaries that differ between IMR-90 and K562 it recovers 0.383 of the contrasts against 0.024-0.264 for all seven comparison methods; it ranks first at every point of a 25-point threshold grid and in all six cell-line pairs, and the remaining methods are ranked differently from pooled correlation. EpiInsula provides a framework for predicting chromatin organisation on a continuous scale from routinely available epigenomic assays. Availability: https://github.com/Yin-Shen/EpiInsula.

title: Transcriptional Regulation of the Meiotic Cohesin Subunit RAD21L by Methylation of Two CpG Islands in Its Promoter and Characterization of Its Interactions with Histones.
authors: Dalai, Wuyun; Saeki, Keiichi; Jiya, Wuen; Jin, Xin; Rong, Mei
abstract: The meiosis-specific cohesin alpha-kleisin subunits REC8 and RAD21L regulate higher-order chromatin organization and germline-specific transcription in male germ cells. Rad21l exhibits high, testis-specific expression in mice, but the epigenetic mechanisms governing its promoter activity and those underlying its chromatin targeting and anchoring remain unclear. To address these questions, we investigated Rad21l using dual-luciferase reporter assays, in vitro methylation, bisulfite sequencing, molecular docking, transcriptome sequencing, and co-immunoprecipitation. We identified a distal regulatory region and mapped the core promoter of Rad21l to the -228 to -3 bp region. We further demonstrated that methylation of the promoter CpG islands represses its transcription. Molecular docking simulations suggested that KLF4 could bind a promoter sequence containing CpG5 and that methylation would not disrupt this interaction. Methylation was hypothesized to induce conformational remodeling of KLF4, shift its ability to recruit cofactors, and thereby enable bidirectional transcriptional regulation. Co-immunoprecipitation confirmed the co-occurrence of alpha-kleisin proteins with the meiosis-specific histone H1t and histone H3, detected modified H3 forms including H3K9me1 and H3S10phos, and showed their association with HP1beta. Histone modifications may regulate interaction affinity through long-range allosteric effects. This study proposes a working model for tissue-specific transcriptional regulation of Rad21l involving CpG methylation and KLF4 and establishes a hypothetical model of histone-dependent RAD21L chromatin anchoring, providing a basis for investigating male meiosis and identifying infertility-related targets.

title: Deciphering Cellular and Spatial Regulatory Identities from Sparse Chromatin Accessibility Landscapes.
authors: Wang, Yunhe; Guo, Songyu; Qian, Jingjing; Liang, Heqiu; Su, Yanchi; Yu, Zhuohan; Li, Xiangtao
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
abstract: Chromatin accessibility profiling provides a powerful view of regulatory landscapes across heterogeneous biological systems, enabling the investigation of cell-state diversity and spatially organized regulatory programs. However, deciphering meaningful regulatory identities from sparse and noisy accessibility landscapes remains challenging, particularly for closely related cellular states and neighboring regulatory domains. Unlike transcriptomic measurements, chromatin accessibility does not directly capture canonical marker expression, and regulatory identities must therefore be inferred from indirect evidence, including gene activity scores, transcription factor motif activity, and reference-based annotation. These signals often become ambiguous, limiting the reliability of unsupervised clustering followed by post-hoc interpretation. Here, we present CASSIA (Chromatin Accessibility Semi-Supervised Identity-Aware representation learning), a unified label-guided framework for decoding cellular and spatial regulatory identities from chromatin accessibility landscapes. CASSIA leverages limited high-confidence anchors to learn informative accessibility representations while preserving intrinsic regulatory structures. The framework integrates a binary accessibility denoising autoencoder, a Jensen-Shannon divergence-based clustering constraint, and a similarity difference-aware triplet objective; spatial neighborhood consistency is further incorporated to preserve regulatory organization when spatial information is available. Across diverse chromatin accessibility datasets, CASSIA reconstructs cellular and spatial regulatory identities with improved agreement to biological annotations and tissue organization compared with representative baselines. Identity-associated accessible regions and transcription factor activity profiles reveal distinct regulatory programs underlying inferred identities, demonstrating that CASSIA transforms sparse accessibility landscapes into interpretable cellular and tissue-level regulatory maps.

title: Decoding Conformational Dynamics and Hyperactivity of Histone H3K36 N-Methyltransferase in Oncogenic Mutations via tICA and Markov State Modeling.
authors: Shah, Tejas; Heidari, Sahar; Rydzewski, Jakub; Torabifard, Hedieh
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
abstract: NSD2 is a histone methyltransferase that modifies lysine 36 in histone H3 (H3K36), playing a central role in chromatin organization and transcriptional regulation. Oncogenic mutations, such as E1099K and T1150A in NSD2, have been associated with hyperactive methylation, but the molecular mechanisms underlying this gain of function remain poorly understood. In this study, we performed all-atom molecular dynamics simulations of NSD2 bound to the nucleosome in wild type (WT), E1099K, T1150A, and the E1099K/T1150A double mutant. Analysis of MD simulations reveals that the global dynamics of the enzymes remain unaltered upon mutations. The time-lagged independent component analysis and Markov state modeling uncovered fundamental differences in free-energy landscapes among the variants. The WT NSD2 exhibited energetically and kinetically unfavorable transitions between the macrostates along with extended enzyme-substrate distances. On the other hand, the mutant systems demonstrate reduced SAM-H3K36 distances with modified energy landscapes that facilitate transitions or favor prolonged occupancy of catalytically competent states. Importantly, the mutations reorganize the network of intramolecular contacts around the catalytic site, SAM-binding pocket, and histone-binding interface, optimizing substance engagement geometry. These findings are consistent with experimental observations of enhanced catalytic activity and suggest that oncogenic mutations promote hyperactivity through strategic reorganization of conformational dynamics rather than simple destabilization, balancing local flexibility with global stability to enhance catalytic efficiency. Our results provide mechanistic insights into NSD2 dysregulation in cancer and establish a framework to develop novel therapeutics that target the enzyme's dynamic landscape.

title: simPIC: flexible simulation of single-cell ATAC-seq paired-insertion counts from individuals to populations.
authors: Chugh, Sagrika; Shim, Heejung; McCarthy, Davis J
abstract: Single-cell Assay for Transposase Accessible Chromatin (scATAC-seq) is increasingly used at population scale to study how genetic variation shapes chromatin accessibility. Method development is limited by the lack of flexible simulation tools with known ground truth. Here, we present simPIC, a fast, memory-efficient framework for simulating realistic single-cell ATAC-seq count data across individuals and populations. simPIC models cell groups, batch effects, and genotype-dependent accessibility variation, enabling evaluation of population-scale methods, including chromatin accessibility quantitative trait locus mapping. Across multiple datasets and cell types, simPIC closely matches real data distributions while scaling to cohort sizes impractical for current tools.

title: Population epigenomics of plant DNA methylation: perspectives for molecular breeding.
authors: Long, Xi; Zheng, Juyun; Fang, Lei; Zhao, Ting
journal: Journal of Zhejiang University. Science. B
abstract: DNA methylation, a key epigenetic modification, contributes to regulatory diversity in plants and plays important roles in phenotypic plasticity and environmental adaptation. Recent population epigenomic studies have revealed extensive methylation variation across plant genomes, characterized genomic distribution and genetic architecture, and demonstrated both its dependence on and partial independence from underlying DNA sequence variation. These studies have further linked methylation variation to gene expression regulation, domestication, local adaptation, and complex trait variation through integrative analyses and epigenome-wide association research. Advances in high-throughput sequencing have enabled the generation of population-scale plant methylomes across natural accessions, wild relatives, landraces, and breeding germplasm, providing new avenues to systematically investigate epigenomic diversity and its functional consequences. In parallel, public methylome resources, epigenomic databases, and multi-omics analytical platforms are accelerating comparative and cross-species analyses of plant epigenomic variation. Future efforts that integrate population methylomes with genomics, transcriptomics, chromatin accessibility, three-dimensional genome organization, deep learning-based analytical frameworks, and targeted epigenome editing are expected to facilitate the discovery of epigenetic breeding markers, promoting the application of epigenomic variation in crop improvement.

title: Unlocking the Regulatory Genome by ARGUS: An Evidence-Constrained Agentic Framework for Interpreting Single Nucleotide Variants.
authors: Dutta, Pratik; Obusan, Matthew B; Chao, Max; Sathian, Rekha; Papineni, Nimisha; Davuluri, Ramana V
abstract: Over 90% of disease-associated variants from genome-wide association studies fall in noncoding regulatory regions, yet their functional interpretation remains a central open problem in genomic medicine. Large language models prompted to interpret such variants routinely hallucinate transcription factor (TF) binding changes, fabricate experimental support, and assign biological significance to statistically negligible signals. We present ARGUS (Agentic Regulatory Genomics for an Uncertainty-aware Scientist), which strictly separates deterministic biological computation from LLM-mediated reasoning. ARGUS wraps 458 DNABERT-based TF binding models in a hypothesis-directed investigation loop where a planner selects evidence sources based on current uncertainty, a verifier deterministically interprets each observation, and intermediate results change the investigation path. On variant rs6983267 at the 8q24 cancer risk locus, the same planner produces four divergent trajectories for four TFs. FOXA1 is rescued in 3 steps when real ADASTRA allele-specific binding data (15 experiments, FDR = 0.030) reveals a model false negative masked by saturation (both alleles predicted at near-maximal binding, leaving the model unable to resolve allelic differences). KLF6 traverses 8 steps across ADASTRA, JASPAR motif analysis, and ENCODE cCRE regulatory annotation before abstaining due to mixed indirect evidence. RAD21 abstains in 8 steps after ADASTRA returns a powered but nonsignificant allelic test (5 experiments, FDR = 0.65), and SP1, which shares FOXA1's saturated retained prediction, abstains because no direct experimental evidence exists at this locus. All trajectories are produced from real data against local ADASTRA, JASPAR, and ENCODE cCRE evidence sources, with no simulated observations. A comparison of fixed-priority and LLM-mediated planning shows that the LLM planner reaches identical verdicts with fewer tool calls by declining evidence that cannot resolve the claim under test.

title: Comparative analysis of KMT2A fusions in human models of acute myeloid leukemia.
authors: Safa-Tahar-Henni, Safia; Milan, Thomas; DesCoteaux, Thomas; Roques, Elodie; Bonnet-Magnaval, Florence; Osborne, Michael J; Bresson, Eva; Mathien, Simon; Chazin, Walter J; Hebert, Josee; Borden, Katherine L B; Najmanovich, Rafael; Cellot, Sonia; Barabe, Frederic; Wilhelm, Brian T
abstract: Pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (AML) frequently involves chromosomal rearrangements, particularly KMT2A (MLL) gene fusions, with the KMT2A-MLLT4 (KM4-AML) fusion being highly aggressive and associated with poor prognosis. This study presents a comparative analysis of transcriptomic and epigenetic profiles between human leukemia models harboring KM4-AML and KMT2A-MLLT3 (KM3-AML) fusions. Transcriptomic signatures of KM4-AML models closely resembled those of patient samples, underscoring the model's clinical relevance. Epigenetic analysis revealed distinct chromatin accessibility and methylation patterns between KM4-AML and KM3-AML, particularly in enhancer regions linked to aggressive leukemia phenotypes. PROM1 was identified as a potential biomarker for KM4-AML, with its overexpression correlating with poor prognosis. Furthermore, high-throughput drug screening identified dopamine receptor antagonists (DRAs) as promising therapeutic candidates showing selective response for KM4-AML models. Docking simulations and NMR assays confirmed favorable binding interactions between DRAs and S100A8, S100A9 and ANXA6. These findings provide insights into the molecular mechanisms driving KM4-AML and offer potential therapeutic avenues for treatment.

title: Integrative Transcriptomics and Machine Learning Identify Temporal Stress Signatures and Astrocytic Neurocan Associated With Hypothalamic Injury.
authors: Zhu, Weihao; Li, Chenyu; He, Mengting; Shi, Rui; Liu, Xia; Shi, Weibo; Cong, Bin
abstract: BACKGROUND: Stress-related neurological dysfunction evolves dynamically, but molecular markers distinguishing stress stages remain limited. We aimed to characterize temporal hypothalamic transcriptomic changes and identify molecular signatures for stress-stage discrimination. METHODS: Whole-transcriptome sequencing was performed in mouse hypothalami after stress. Differential expression, temporal clustering, co-expression network analysis, and machine learning were integrated to identify stress-associated mRNA and miRNA signatures. Candidate markers were validated by RT-qPCR and single-nucleus RNA sequencing. Ncan function was further evaluated by protein supplementation, perineuronal net analysis, behavioral testing, and regulatory network analysis. RESULTS: mRNAs exhibited strong temporal sensitivity and captured stage-specific transcriptional remodeling, whereas miRNAs primarily reflected stress regardless of duration. A six-mRNA signature (Ncan, Mt2, Nab2, Ptch1, and Catspere1/Catspere2) accurately distinguished control, acute stress, and chronic stress (accuracy, 1.000), while an 11-miRNA signature robustly classified stress states (accuracy, 0.944). Both signatures were validated by RT-qPCR and nested cross-validation, with accuracies of 0.898 and 0.890, respectively. Ncan was consistently top-ranked, predominantly expressed in astrocytes, progressively downregulated by stress, and its supplementation restored PNNs and alleviated depressive-like behaviors. Virtual Ncan knockout disrupted the stress network, with Ctcf predicted as its upstream regulator. CONCLUSION: Our study identifies distinct stress-stage and stress-state transcriptomic signatures and highlights astrocytic Ncan as a candidate biomarker that may contribute to stress-induced neural injury by regulating PNN homeostasis.

title: DeepCNet: A multimodal deep learning model for predicting cell type-specific gene expression and promoter-enhancer interactions from single-cell multiome data.
authors: Jin, Weijia; Zhao, Fengdi; Ma, Xin; Lu, Qing; Esser, Karyn A; Sun, Ramon C; Chen, Li
abstract: Understanding promoter-enhancer (PE) interactions is essential for elucidating gene regulation mechanisms. Although existing computational methods leverage DNA sequence to predict gene expression, many were developed primarily for bulk-level genomic data and emphasize predictive accuracy rather than regulatory inference. Here, we propose DeepCNet, a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts cell type-specific gene expression and infers cell type-specific PE interactions, enabling the construction of transcription factor gene regulatory networks (TF-GRNs) from single-cell multiome data. Evaluated on two single-cell multiome datasets from blood and brain tissues, DeepCNet consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in predicting cell type-specific gene expression. Importantly, PE interactions inferred by DeepCNet showed greater concordance with orthogonal chromatin interaction and CRISPR perturbation data than competing approaches. Analysis of cell type-specific GRNs identified TF hubs and highlighted both cell type-specific and shared regulatory programs. DeepCNet further extends to two-condition single-cell multiome studies, enabling the identification of differential PE interactions and characterization of TF-GRN alterations across conditions. As an illustrative application, we applied DeepCNet to single-cell multiome data from one Alzheimer's disease (AD) and one healthy control sample, identifying candidate differential PE interactions at AD risk loci and candidate TF hubs associated with AD-related pathways. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of DeepCNet to characterize transcriptional regulatory programs and cooperative TF interactions underlying cell type- and condition-specific gene expression.

title: HiC-LEGO: Biologically Guided High-Resolution 3D Genome Reconstruction Preserves Chromatin Organization at Kilobase Resolution.
authors: Pandeya, Abhishek; Chowdhury, Md Fahimul Kabir; Oluwadare, Oluwatosin
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) chromosome reconstruction from Hi-C contact maps remains challenging because genome organization is hierarchical and fine-resolution models must reconcile local structure with chromosome-scale constraints. Here we present HiC-LEGO, a domain-aware hierarchical framework integrating ensemble chromatin domains with graph-based structural learning and progressive chromosome assembly. By combining ensemble domain selection with hierarchical reconstruction, HiC-LEGO reduces dependence on individual domain definitions while maintaining local organization during chromosome-scale assembly. Across five human cell lines at 5-kb resolution, HiC-LEGO achieves higher reconstruction concordance than evaluated state-of-the-art methods while better preserving domain organization. At 1-kb resolution, HiC-LEGO reconstructs complete GM12878 chromosome 8 and recovers close spatial proximity between an epigenomically supported distal MYC enhancer and its promoter. Reconstructions from 5-kb Micro-C data show that 249 experimentally defined RCMC microcompartment interactions at the Ppm1g locus occupy compact 3D configurations. In the breast cancer dataset, HiC-LEGO reconstructs structures that maintain stable TAD organization across healthy breast, primary tumors, and liver metastases, while revealing greater inter-patient structural heterogeneity in malignant pleural effusion samples. Pore-C validation shows that experimentally observed multi-way contacts spanning 1-5 Mb are enriched in compact reconstructed configurations across all 23 chromosomes. Thus, HiC-LEGO preserves regulatory interactions, disease-associated chromatin organization and higher-order spatial relationships beyond pairwise contact-map concordance.
